While it's great to plant deterrent plants like marigolds, and trap crops to lure pests away from your veggies, another piece of the puzzle is planting things that draw in predatory insects. Consider putting in plants that also attract beneficial predator insects. I leave wasp nests alone around my yard as long as they aren't in an area that we frequent. Because while I'm out in the garden I'll see them crawling around on the underside's of the leaves of my veggies looking for caterpillars, cabbage worms, and other bugs to take back to their nest.
Very comprehensive list. Thanks. I coincidentally have some of these sprouting.
Yeah rosemary, lavender thyme and time spring to mind.

Any alliums (spring onions, garlic, leeks, onions, chives) are great. I plant them in between rows in my square-foot garden - they are zero-maintenance, they take up hardly any room, and their feeding habits do not compete with other (non-allium) vegetables. They don't smell bad to us, but they confuse flying insects by masking the scent of your other plants.

There is also the anti-companion thing to watch out for - e.g. avoid planting mustard greens near cruciferous veggies.
